key_insight: Evolving molten-zone geometry changes local solidification velocity, helping explain chemical segregation in Ni–Mn–Ga beyond ideal Scheil–Pfann behaviour.
engineering_relevance: Sapphire-confined optical floating-zone growth improves reproducibility and macroscopic geometry control, while modelling supports optimisation toward more homogeneous crystals.
method: Stabilise the optically heated molten zone inside a transparent sapphire crucible.
Couple transient COMSOL finite-element heat transfer to an effective molten-zone mass balance.
Reconstruct solidification-front evolution and longitudinal composition profiles.
evidence_signal: EBSD of a quenched interface independently supports the calculated front geometry, and the coupled model reproduces dominant features of measured composition profiles.
watch_item: The abstract reports no quantitative prediction errors, so reconstruction accuracy and transferability to other growth conditions remain unclear.
paper_title: Finite-element reconstruction of molten-zone dynamics and chemical segregation in optical floating-zone grown Ni--Mn--Ga
